question.problem:
Solve the following congruence:

$$
5x-4≡34\,(\text{mod}\,18)
$$

*Hint: You may wish to use trial and error to find the appropriate multiplicative inverse.*
question.worked_solution:
First, we reduce our congruence to a congruence of the form $ax≡b,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x-4 & ≡34\, & (\text{mod}\,18) \\ 5x-4+4 & ≡34+4\, & (\text{mod}\,18) \\ 5x & ≡38\, & (\text{mod}\,18) \\ 5x & ≡2\cdot 18+2\, & (\text{mod}\,18) \\ 5x & ≡2\, & (\text{mod}\,18)\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that a linear congruence $ax≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)$ has a unique solution modulo $n$ if and only if $\text{gcd}(a,n)=1.$

In the given congruence, we have $a=5$ and $n=18$, and

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(5,18)=1.
$$

So, our congruence does indeed have a unique solution.

To find the solution, we need to multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $5\,(\text{mod}\,18).$ To find the inverse of $5\,(\text{mod}\,18)$, we compute the exponents of $5\,(\text{mod}\,18)$ until we get a result of $1\,(\text{mod}\,18):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{5}^{2} & ≡25≡1\cdot 18+7≡7 &  & (\text{mod}\,18) \\ {5}^{3} & ≡7\cdot 5≡35≡1\cdot 18+17≡17 &  & (\text{mod}\,18) \\ {5}^{4} & ≡17\cdot 5≡85≡4\cdot 18+13≡13 &  & (\text{mod}\,18) \\ {5}^{5} & ≡13\cdot 5≡65≡3\cdot 18+11≡11 &  & (\text{mod}\,18) \\ {5}^{6} & ≡11\cdot 5≡55≡3\cdot 18+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,18)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $11\cdot 5≡1\,(\text{mod}\,18),$ which means that $11$ is the multiplicative inverse of $5$ (modulo $18$).

Now, multiplying both sides of our congruence by $11,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x & ≡2 &  & (\text{mod}\,18) \\ 11\cdot 5x & ≡11\cdot 2 &  & (\text{mod}\,18) \\ (11\cdot 5)x & ≡22 &  & (\text{mod}\,18) \\ 1\cdot x & ≡4+1\cdot 18 &  & (\text{mod}\,18) \\ x & ≡4 &  & (\text{mod}\,18)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x≡4\,(\text{mod}\,18).$
